classification.difficultyReason: Select two new viewpoints for each assembly and transfer the L-shaped base and stacked cube consistently to isometric paper. This requires tracking arm lengths, the stack's attachment point and visible subdivisions through routine spatial rotations.

content.prompt: Draw two different isometric drawings of each of the following.

spec.description: Five unit cubes: four in an L-shaped base and one above the short arm's end. White face masks hide occluded edges; visible unit subdivisions remain.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied assembly only; no alternative view.

spec.description: Two separate isometric dot regions for the requested drawings.
spec.mathematics: Triangular dot lattice with equal spacing in the three isometric directions.

answer.short: Sample answers shown. Both drawings represent the same five-cube assembly.
answer.worked: Keep the four-cube L-shaped base and the cube stacked at the end of its short arm. Draw the assembly from two different viewpoints, retaining equal unit edges, parallel edge directions and visible cube subdivisions.

spec.description: Two sample isometric orientations of the five-cube L-shaped assembly.
spec.mathematics: First view swaps the horizontal arm directions. Second view rotates the original occupied cells through a quarter turn around the vertical axis.

spec.description: Seven unit cubes: two perpendicular base arms meet at the foreground corner, with another cube stacked at that corner. One arm extends three cubes beyond the corner and the other extends two.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied assembly only; no alternative view.

spec.description: Two separate isometric dot regions for the requested drawings.
spec.mathematics: Triangular dot lattice with equal spacing in the three isometric directions.

answer.short: Sample answers shown. Both drawings represent the same seven-cube assembly.
answer.worked: Retain the six-cube L-shaped base: the arms extend three and two cubes beyond their shared corner. Keep the seventh cube above that corner. Change the viewing direction and draw only the visible edges, preserving all visible unit subdivisions.

spec.description: Two sample orientations retaining the unequal base arms and the upper corner cube.
spec.mathematics: Both figures have seven cubes. The second uses the quarter-turn transformation (x,y,z) to (y,-x,z).
